# Zain Dana Harper: tools in plain terms

> Ten tools by Zain Dana Harper, each as a short record: what it does, who it is
> for, how to try it, what it does not do, its current version and licence, and
> where to read more. Versions are current as of 2026-10-23. The short index is
> https://harperz9.github.io/llms.txt and the full product registry, with dated
> evidence for each claim, is https://harperz9.github.io/system/systems.json.

Every tool below runs on your own computer. None needs an account with the
author. Source for each is on GitHub under https://github.com/HarperZ9.

## Flywheel

Version 1.9.0. Licence FSL-1.1-MIT. Python 3.11 or newer, no third-party
runtime dependencies.

- What it does: runs AI tasks on any hosted or local model behind one
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint on your machine, checks the values in an answer
  against the source that decides them (a tax table, a formulary, a court
  calendar, a script you supply), and records every step on a hash-chained
  ledger that can be checked again later, offline.
- Who it is for: developers and teams who use AI agents or model output and
  need to show which parts of an answer were checked, and against what.
- Try it: `python -m pip install flywheel-verify` then `flywheel gate`.
  `flywheel code` runs a coding agent in your terminal.
- What it does not do: it does not decide that an answer is true beyond the
  sources you give it. It reports which fields agree, which disagree, and which
  nothing could confirm. By default the coding agent asks before it writes or
  runs anything.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/flywheel.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/flywheel , https://pypi.org/project/flywheel-verify/ ,
  docs https://harperz9.github.io/flywheel/docs/

## Articulate

Version 0.16.0. Licence FSL-1.1-MIT. Python 3.9 or newer, standard library only.

- What it does: checks prose on your computer and names each writing pattern it
  finds and the line it sits on: stacked hedges, marketing words, corporate
  verbs, contrast framing, rule-of-three lists, em dashes. A profile for each
  kind of writing (procedure, commit, readme, research, essay, narrative)
  decides which findings block.
- Who it is for: anyone who writes documentation, READMEs, release notes,
  essays or commit messages and wants a style check in a terminal, an editor
  (LSP), CI (SARIF) or an AI agent (MCP).
- Try it: `python -m pip install articulate-writing` then
  `articulate check README.md --profile readme --gate`.
- What it does not do: it is a style checker, not an authorship detector. On
  183 texts of known origin it flagged all 84 AI texts and 57 of 75 human texts
  (76%, 95% interval 65% to 84%). It needs no model, account or API key.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/articulate.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/articulate , https://pypi.org/project/articulate-writing/

## Daylight Commons

Version 3.6.2. Licence AGPL-3.0-only. A browser extension for Chrome, Edge,
Brave and Firefox 128 or later, plus a command line for saved threads.

- What it does: rest the pointer on a reply on X, YouTube, Reddit, Facebook,
  Instagram, Bluesky, Threads, TikTok or a Mastodon server you turn it on for,
  and a window shows where the platform places the account, signs of
  coordination, how the account posts, how the reply argues, and whether a
  fact-checker has reviewed the claim.
- Who it is for: people who read replies and comment threads and want to know
  who is talking before they weigh what is said.
- Try it: download the release for your browser from
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/daylight-commons/releases/latest and load it
  unpacked; the install page is https://harperz9.github.io/daylight-commons/install.html .
  The command line runs as `node bin/radar.mjs analyze saved-thread.html`.
- What it does not do: it shows signs and their sources; a sign of coordination
  is evidence to weigh, not a verdict on a person. Firefox removes the
  temporary add-on on restart until a signed build is published.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/daylight.html ,
  https://harperz9.github.io/daylight-commons/install.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/daylight-commons

## EMET

Version 1.3.1. Licence MPL-2.0 for 1.3.1 and earlier; AGPL-3.0-only from the
next release. Python 3.8 or newer, no dependencies. Ports in Rust, Node.js and Go.

- What it does: checks whether a file still matches the SHA-256 you recorded
  for it and answers MATCH, DRIFT or UNVERIFIABLE. It seals a verdict into a
  small JSON receipt that anyone can check on their own machine.
- Who it is for: anyone who has to show that a document, dataset or prompt a
  model, a reviewer or a pipeline read is the same one that was approved.
- Try it: `python -m pip install emet`, then `emet anchor report.md` and
  `emet verify report.md`.
- What it does not do: it compares bytes. It does not judge whether the content
  of a matching file is correct. With no recorded hash it answers UNVERIFIABLE
  and exits 2 rather than guessing.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/emet.html , https://github.com/HarperZ9/emet ,
  https://pypi.org/project/emet/

## BuildLang

Version 1.10.0. Licence AGPL-3.0-only. Written in Rust.

- What it does: a compiled language where a function's type lists its side
  effects, such as file, network and C access, so a call that reads a file
  without declaring it fails to compile. It builds native binaries through C
  and emits HLSL and GLSL shaders; SPIR-V, LLVM IR, WebAssembly and other
  backends are experimental.
- Who it is for: systems and graphics programmers who want the compiler to show
  what a piece of code is allowed to touch.
- Try it: `cargo install buildlang`, then `buildc doctor`.
- What it does not do: the experimental backends are not production paths; the
  C backend is.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/buildlang.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/buildlang , https://crates.io/crates/buildlang

## raw-native

Version 0.8.0. Licence FSL-1.1-MIT. C++23; Windows, Linux and WebAssembly, with
optional D3D12 and WebGPU builds.

- What it does: renders a 3D scene on the CPU and computes ambient occlusion two
  ways, with the screen-space shortcut real-time engines use and by ray
  tracing, then writes both images, a per-pixel error map and a JSON
  certificate with a verdict: verified inside the tolerance, refuted outside.
- Who it is for: graphics developers who need a reference to test an occlusion,
  shading or colour implementation against, or renders that come out the same
  on every machine.
- Try it: build from https://github.com/HarperZ9/raw-native and run
  `raw_native_cli --out ./out`.
- What it does not do: the default view comes back refuted (RMSE 0.135 against
  a tolerance of 0.12); the record keeps that result.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/raw.html , https://github.com/HarperZ9/raw-native

## Telos

Version 0.9.0. Licence FSL-1.1-MIT. Node.js 20 or newer, no npm dependencies.

- What it does: a local MCP server and command line for AI agents. It lets an
  agent read web pages and public APIs, triage a failed GitHub Actions run,
  check an HTML page for accessibility and size problems, and drive a browser
  or Windows apps after you grant access. Gated actions go to a hash-chained log.
- Who it is for: people running agents in MCP hosts such as Claude Code, Codex
  or the OpenAI Agents SDK who want those agents to act with a record.
- Try it: `npx -y project-telos-mcp` in an MCP host config. A `tools/list` call
  against 0.9.0 returns 50 tools.
- What it does not do: nothing that controls a browser or app runs until you
  issue a grant. Install it as `project-telos-mcp`; the npm name `telos`
  belongs to an unrelated package.
- Links: https://github.com/HarperZ9/telos , https://www.npmjs.com/package/project-telos-mcp

## learn

Version 2.3.0. Fair Source licence. Node.js 20 or newer, no dependencies.

- What it does: a study planner for the terminal and for agents over MCP. You
  list your objectives and record each practice attempt; it tells you what is
  due for review, which mistakes keep coming back, what order to practise in,
  and whether you have reached mastery.
- Who it is for: anyone studying for a course, an exam or a certification who is
  comfortable in a terminal, and developers who want an agent to plan study
  sessions.
- Try it: `npx -y @harperz9/learn@2.3.0 tutor plan mysession --topic "derivatives" --objectives "power-rule,chain-rule"`.
- What it does not do: it never answers a graded question. Its course engine
  stops at every graded step for you to do yourself.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/learn.html , https://github.com/HarperZ9/learn ,
  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@harperz9/learn

## open-archives

Version 0.1.0, not yet released. Licence AGPL-3.0-only. Python 3.11 or newer,
standard library only; media work uses ffmpeg.

- What it does: searches free archives and museum collections with one query,
  from archive.org and Wikimedia Commons to the Met and NASA, downloads the
  items you pick, and cuts clips, audio loops and textures from them. Every
  item carries its licence class and rights basis.
- Who it is for: filmmakers, game and design makers who need period reference
  images, b-roll, sound and textures they can ship.
- Try it: `git clone https://github.com/HarperZ9/open-archives`, then
  `python -m openarchives search "cotton mill" --media image --from 1837 --to 1955`.
- What it does not do: it records the rights basis it finds; a licence you hold
  or a fair-use call is yours to record with `rights`.
- Links: https://github.com/HarperZ9/open-archives

## discover

Version 0.1.2. Licence AGPL-3.0-only. Python 3.11 or newer, standard library only.

- What it does: before a release, checks that people can find a project: a
  README that opens with what it does and a command to run, GitHub description
  and topics, package keywords, CITATION.cff, page titles and descriptions,
  JSON-LD, sitemap, robots access for search crawlers, llms.txt, and video
  chapters and hashtags. It scores the result, lists fixes, and with `--gate`
  fails CI.
- Who it is for: maintainers who ship open-source tools, sites or videos and
  want them found by the people they serve.
- Try it: `python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/HarperZ9/discover@v0.1.2"`
  then `discover repo . --gate`.
- What it does not do: it checks form, not merit, and claims no ranking effect.
  Its video check fails engagement bait.
- Links: https://github.com/HarperZ9/discover
